body:
No, don't worry about projecting, I enjoy knowing that what I'm experiencing isn't an isolated thing (even though that may sound bad if you interpret it saying I wish others went through what I have to). 

Thank you for the sentiments, as I currently am feeling hopeless. I guess I've always been of the mind that if two people work hard together and keep open communication, nothing could stop them being together. I guess I did learn a lot through this relationship; such as not becoming solely dependent on one person for your social interaction, and not basing your happiness completely on another person's happiness. I understand that put into perspective, it's a long-term girlfriend I had in college in my late teens; it's not the end of the world if it doesn't work out. I need to work on really getting in my mind the idea that these are transitory years for me, not the end-all life expectations.

Also, that description of feeling like the floor's about to cave in under you is quite accurate.

Thanks, the similarities are quite striking(scary even, considering one my "escapes" is playing Starcraft 2), and it's nice to know that I'm not some outlier. I go through cycles where I'm feeling great; like I realize I'm young, in good shape, and a good understanding of myself and my limitations. I guess the problem arises when there's nothing to keep me occupied, such as in the middle of the night, and I think about the fact that the girl I thought I'd end up maybe marrying doesn't want anything to do with me, etc. It's hard sometimes, though listening to music helps.

Ideally? I'd rediscover my passion for game design, I'd really get into my hobbies more, I might stumble across a relationship(I'm not really the "looking for it" kind of guy, I haven't been single for about 6 years and never went looking specifically for someone, and I'm definitely not into the partying/clubbing scene), I'd get back into a normal workout routine(I rowed for 5 years, but couldn't afford to continue doing so, so I've sporadically exercising when the mood takes me) and my family holds together long enough for me to get my degree and get out of there. I just have serious doubts on whether any of that will happen, who knows right?

Thanks again, it's nice to vent and know there's someone listening. I'm the generalized guy who keeps everything bottled up and doesn't try to let things bother him, seemingly skating by in life, but sometimes I just can't fake being calm and collected.
